text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty HIGH -> inference-queue-surge for service=redwood-inference-autoscale. Trigger: queue_depth > 5k for 5m; latency p95 > 1200ms. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/autoscale-queue-surge :rotating_light:
pd-bot: PD Alert PD-1432 fired -> paging alex (oncall). Escalation policy: 10m -> senior-sre.
alex (oncall): ack. I'm awake, looking now. Impact? any customer-facing errors reported? :eyes:
jo (sre): seeing a spike in dispatcher 503s and inflight queue depth climbing. metrics: desired_replicas=18 current_replicas=6, queue_depth=5.6k. autoscaler logs show repeated scale requests failing.
 tara (eng): pulling autoscaler logs, getting kube-apiserver 429s on scale calls. snippet:
```
2026-03-17T12:07:14Z WARN autoscaler controller callScaleUp failed status=429 message="Too Many Requests"
2026-03-17T12:07:21Z INFO reconcile loop next in 30s
```
maya (prodops): also seeing spot pool churn in us-west-2, a bunch of spot terminations 1m ago; reserved pool nearly empty. cloud quotas look normal but provider throttling is high.
alex (oncall): ok hypothesis: provider API throttling + spot churn => autoscaler cannot provision nodes quickly enough, so pods stuck Pending. Customer impact = increased errors and latency. Plan: 1) manual nodepool scale to warm up capacity 2) redirect some traffic -> dedicated-reserve model 3) open PD ticket to cloud provider if provider throttling persists. Who can run manual nodepool scale?
tara (eng): I can. Starting manual scale to +30 nodes on autoscale-pool now: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize autoscale-pool --size=36 --zone=us-west2-b` (running).
jo (sre): while that runs, I'll enable temporary request-throttling in the ingress to slow new work: flip feature-flag `inference.throttle_backlog=true` in prod routing. Applying now.
alex (oncall): good. I'm opening a mitigation doc and pinging customers team to prepare comms. @maya can you take provider-side escalation? Also add a temporary fallback route to dedicated-reserve (route id: reserve-west-1)
maya (prodops): escalating to provider Support case CASE-9981, including apiserver 429 traces + spot churn metrics. Fallback route enabled to reserve-west-1, traffic diverted ~30%.
tara (eng): manual scale returned: new instances arriving, pods scheduling. autoscaler logs show fewer 429s now but still some 429 retries. Replicas moving from 6 -> 22.
jo (sre): queue depth starting to drop: 5.6k -> 3.1k -> 1.1k over 8m. 503s down from 12% -> 2%.
alex (oncall): marking PD alert acknowledged and in mitigation. If we hit stable queue < 500 for 10m we'll close. Keeping senior-sre on-call in loop.
pd-bot: PD PD-1432 acknowledged by alex (oncall). Escalation halted.
incident-bot: Note: created incident doc https://incidents/PD-1432 with timeline and runbook steps.
maya (prodops): provider responded: provider-side throttling due to control-plane spike; they raised limits and will monitor. Spot churn subsided.
jo (sre): continuing to watch autoscaler retries; recommend follow-up: add exponential backoff on scale calls, add reserved warm pool, and increase control-plane API quota where possible.
tara (eng): I'll file a PR for warm pool + backoff heuristics and link in incident doc.
alex (oncall): thanks all. Keeping thread open until stable window met. will update status when PD closed. :white_check_mark:
